# 1 Clement Chapter 51 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 51

---

## Council Notes

**On "assaults" / "stratagems" (v.1):** EMET: "assaults." LOGOS: "stratagems." The Greek *epiboulai* means plots/schemes laid against someone. "Stratagems" (LOGOS) captures the planned, cunning quality better than "assaults."

**On "common hope" (v.1):** All agents agree. This is a key ecclesiological phrase — the hope shared by the whole community transcends individual grievance.

**On "fall into torments" / "fall into distress" (v.2):** EMET: "torments." LOGOS: "distress." PNEUMA: "suffer." The Greek *thlipsis* means pressing, affliction, tribulation. "Distress" (LOGOS) is broad enough to cover the range.

**On "Death shall be their shepherd" (v.4):** Clement quotes Psalm 49:14 LXX (Psalm 48:15 LXX numbering). All agents preserve the quotation. This is a striking image of death as shepherd — a complete inversion of Psalm 23. The quotation marks should be clear.

**On "drowned" / "swallowed up" (v.5):** EMET: "drowned." LOGOS: "swallowed up." PNEUMA: "swallowed up." The Greek *katepothēsan* is from *katapinō* (to swallow down/engulf). "Swallowed up" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is more vivid and accurate.

---

**51:1** Whatever things we have transgressed, and whatever things we have done through the stratagems of the adversary, let us ask to be forgiven for them. And those who have made themselves leaders of revolt and sedition ought to look to the common hope.

**51:2** For those who conduct themselves in fear and love prefer to fall into distress themselves rather than their neighbors; and they would rather have condemnation fall upon themselves than see the harmony that has been so nobly and righteously handed down to us brought to disgrace.

**51:3** For it is better for a man to confess his transgressions than to harden his heart — as the hearts were hardened of those who made rebellion against Moses the servant of God, whose judgment was made clear.

**51:4** For they went down into Hades alive, and "Death shall be their shepherd."

**51:5** Pharaoh and his army and all the rulers of Egypt, the chariots and their riders, were swallowed up in the Red Sea and perished — for no other reason than that their foolish hearts were hardened after the signs and wonders had been performed in the land of Egypt through Moses the servant of God.

---

*— SOPHIA*
